q: What is the youngest age for a New Jersey special learner permit?
a: 15 and a half, with a parent's consent
b: 16 and a half, with no course needed
d: 16, when enrolled in a behind-the-wheel driving course
exp: The special learner permit starts at 16 and requires enrollment in a behind-the-wheel course at a high school or licensed driving school.

q: At what age can you get a New Jersey examination permit without going through a driving school?
exp: The examination permit is for applicants at least 17 and does not require a driving school course.

q: How many questions are on the New Jersey knowledge test?
exp: The MVC knowledge test has 50 multiple choice questions.

q: How many of the 50 knowledge test questions must you answer correctly to pass in New Jersey?
exp: You need 80 percent, which is 40 of the 50 questions.

q: Before the road test, how many hours of supervised practice must a New Jersey permit holder under 21 complete?
a: At least 40 hours, including 10 at night
b: At least 50 hours, including 10 in darkness
c: At least 50 hours, including 15 at night
d: At least 65 hours, including 10 at night
exp: Permit holders under 21 must log at least 50 hours of practice driving, 10 of them during darkness.

q: How long must a New Jersey permit holder under 21 practice under supervision before taking the road test?
exp: Under 21, supervised driving lasts at least six months after the permit is validated. At 21 or older it is three months.

q: Who may supervise a New Jersey permit driver under 21?
a: Any licensed driver at least 18 with one year of experience
b: A licensed driver at least 25 with one year of experience
c: A parent or guardian of any age with a valid license
d: A New Jersey driver at least 21, licensed for three years
exp: The supervisor must be at least 21, hold a New Jersey license and have been licensed for at least three years, and must sit in the front seat.

q: During which hours may a New Jersey probationary driver under 21 not drive, unless an exemption applies?
exp: Permit and probationary drivers under 21 may not drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5 a.m., except for work or religious activities with proof.

q: Without a parent or guardian in the car, how many passengers besides dependents may a New Jersey probationary driver under 21 carry?
exp: Only one passenger is allowed beyond parents, guardians and dependents, unless a parent or guardian is in the car.

q: Where must a New Jersey permit or probationary driver under 21 display the red GDL decals?
a: On the front and rear license plates
c: On the front license plate only
exp: Kyleigh's Law requires a red reflective decal on the upper left corner of both the front and rear license plates.

q: How many hours of behind-the-wheel lessons does a New Jersey special learner permit holder take with a licensed instructor before practice driving with family?
exp: The special learner path starts with 6 hours of instruction in a dual-control car with a licensed driving instructor.

q: A New Jersey driver fails the knowledge test. How long must they wait before retesting?
exp: After a failed knowledge test, the MVC lets you retest in 7 days.

q: A New Jersey driver fails the road test. How long must they wait before retesting?
exp: After a failed road test you must wait at least 14 days before you retest.

q: What vision standard must a New Jersey applicant meet?
a: At least 20/40 in each eye, without lenses
b: At least 20/70 in the better eye
c: At least 20/50 in each eye, with or without lenses
exp: Vision passes at 20/50 or better in each eye, with or without glasses or contacts. With sight in only one eye, that eye must reach 20/50.

q: A New Jersey applicant fails the vision test. What happens next?
a: A doctor completes form ST-14, which the applicant brings back
b: The applicant must wait one year to retest
c: The applicant may take the knowledge test anyway
d: The applicant is given a daytime-only license
exp: If you fail the MVC vision test, your doctor fills out form ST-14 and you return it to the testing center.

q: How many ID points must a New Jersey permit applicant prove with identity documents?
exp: The MVC's 6 Points of ID system requires documents that add up to at least 6 points.

q: How many proofs of New Jersey address are needed for a standard license?
exp: A standard license needs one proof of residential address; a REAL ID needs two.

q: How many proofs of address does a New Jersey REAL ID require?
exp: REAL ID needs two proofs of address, one more than a standard license.

q: Is a REAL ID required to drive in New Jersey?
b: No, it is optional; a standard license is valid for driving
d: Only for drivers who drive out of state
exp: REAL ID is not mandatory. A standard license still lets you drive; it is no longer accepted to board a domestic flight.

q: How much extra does a New Jersey REAL ID cost compared with a standard license?
exp: A REAL ID costs $35 compared with $24 for a standard license, so it is $11 more.

q: What is the MVC fee for a New Jersey examination permit for a car?
exp: The auto examination permit costs $10.

q: What does a pair of New Jersey GDL decals cost?
exp: Decals are sold in pairs for $4 at MVC agencies.

q: What is the fine for breaking a New Jersey GDL restriction, such as the passenger limit or the decal rule?
exp: Violating any permit or probationary license condition, including decals, carries a $100 fine.

q: May a New Jersey probationary driver under 21 talk on a phone using a hands-free device?
b: No, hand-held and hands-free devices are both banned except in an emergency
c: Yes, but only with a parent in the car
exp: Permit and probationary drivers may not use any interactive wireless device, hand-held or hands-free, except in an emergency.

q: What form does a parent, guardian or supervising driver use to certify a New Jersey teen's practice hours?
b: BA-CSD, the Certification of Supervised Driving
exp: Form BA-CSD certifies the 50 practice hours and is presented when the license is issued.

q: What happens if a supervisor submits a false practice-hours certification for a New Jersey permit holder?
a: The permit holder pays a $50 fine
b: The hours are simply logged again
c: The road test is moved back 14 days
d: The permit holder's driving privileges are suspended for six months
exp: A fraudulent certification brings a six-month suspension of the permit holder's driving privileges.

q: How long is a New Jersey GDL examination permit valid?
exp: A GDL examination permit is valid for two years; you must finish the steps in that time or buy a new permit.

q: A New Jersey teen has held a probationary license for one year and is 18. What can they do?
a: Upgrade to a basic license online
b: Nothing; the probationary license lasts until 21
c: Retake the knowledge test for a basic license
d: Take a second road test for a basic license
exp: After one year of unsupervised driving on a probationary license, at 18 or older, you upgrade to a basic license online.

q: Which New Jersey drivers must follow the GDL rules, such as the decals and the 11:01 p.m. limit?
b: Every driver in the first five years
c: Only drivers who failed a test
exp: In New Jersey the GDL restrictions cover permit and probationary drivers under 21, not only teens.

q: A 22-year-old gets a first New Jersey examination permit. How long must they practice under supervision before the road test?
exp: Applicants 21 or older practice under supervision for at least three months before the road test.

q: A 22-year-old New Jersey probationary driver wants to drive with three friends at midnight. Do the GDL night and passenger limits apply?
c: No, those limits apply only to drivers under 21
exp: The night and passenger limits apply to permit and probationary drivers under 21. The device ban still applies to every probationary driver.

q: New Jersey probationary drivers may drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5 a.m. for which reason, with proof?
b: A job or a religious activity
exp: The exemptions are for bona fide employment or religious activities, shown by a signed letter on the employer's or group's letterhead.

q: Which passengers may a New Jersey probationary driver under 21 carry in addition to the one-passenger limit?
a: Any family member, including brothers and sisters
b: Parents, guardians and the driver's own dependents
c: Any passenger who is 21 or older
d: Any classmate who has a license
exp: Parents, guardians and dependents (such as the driver's child, but not a sibling) do not count toward the limit.

q: Within how many days of moving to New Jersey must a new resident transfer an out-of-state license?
c: 60 days, or before it expires if sooner
exp: New residents must transfer within 60 days of moving or before the old license expires, whichever comes first.

q: A new resident holds a valid, non-probationary license from another state. Which tests does New Jersey waive?
exp: With a current, valid, non-probationary license in good standing, the knowledge and road tests are waived.

q: A visitor from another country carries a foreign license and an International Driving Permit. How long may they drive in New Jersey?
exp: Visitors may drive up to one year on a foreign license accompanied by an International Driving Permit.

q: License holders from which two countries can exchange their license in New Jersey without the knowledge and road tests?
exp: New Jersey has reciprocity with Taiwan and South Korea for applicants 18 or older seeking a basic auto license.

q: A New Jersey resident has no Social Security number and no ITIN. How can they meet that requirement for a standard license?
exp: Applicants with neither an SSN nor an ITIN may submit a signed affidavit for a standard license.

q: How long does the New Jersey road test usually take?
exp: The MVC road test takes about 10 to 15 minutes.

q: A New Jersey probationary driver gets two moving violations totaling 4 or more points. What does the MVC require?
exp: Two or more moving violations totaling four or more points during the probationary period lead to the four-hour Probationary Driver Program.

q: How many questions does New Jersey's written knowledge test let you miss and still pass?
exp: With 40 of 50 needed to pass, you can miss at most 10.

q: In how many languages does New Jersey offer the written knowledge test?
exp: The written test is offered in 13 languages; the oral test is in English and Spanish.

q: What is the earliest age to hold a New Jersey probationary license?
exp: Nobody can get a New Jersey license before 17, even on the special learner path.

q: What is the speed limit in a New Jersey school zone during recess or when children are present?
exp: New Jersey law sets 25 mph when passing a school during recess, when children are visible or while they go to or leave school.

q: What happens to fines for moving violations in a posted New Jersey construction zone?
d: They are replaced by points only
exp: Fines for many moving violations double in a construction or repair zone marked by signs or traffic control devices.

q: Do workers have to be present for doubled fines to apply in a posted New Jersey work zone?
c: No, the posted zone is enough
d: Only when a flagger is present
exp: The law requires a construction zone identified by signs or devices; it does not require workers to be present.

q: A New Jersey driver says the doubled-fine sign in a work zone was missing. Is that a defense?
a: No, a missing sign is not a defense
d: Only if the driver took a photo
exp: The law says it is not a defense that a sign was missing, improperly posted, removed or stolen.

q: On which other New Jersey roads do fines double besides work zones?
c: Every road with a 65 mph limit
exp: Doubled fines also apply in designated safe corridors.

q: May you turn left on a red light in New Jersey from a one-way street onto another one-way street?
b: No, left on red is never allowed
c: Yes, if no sign forbids it
exp: New Jersey law allows only right turns on red. A left on red is not allowed, even one-way to one-way.

q: What must you do before turning right on a red light in New Jersey?
a: Slow down and turn if the road looks clear
b: Wait for the light to turn yellow
d: Stop completely, then yield to traffic and pedestrians
exp: Right on red is allowed after a full stop, yielding to other traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk, unless a sign forbids it.

q: When is a right turn on red NOT allowed in New Jersey?
exp: Right on red is allowed after a full stop unless an official sign prohibits it.

q: How far from a New Jersey school bus with flashing red lights must you stop?
exp: Drivers must stop at least 25 feet from a school bus showing flashing red lights.

q: You are on the other side of a divided highway with a barrier when a school bus stops with red lights flashing. What does New Jersey law require?
b: Continue at the posted limit with care
c: Slow to 25 mph or less until you pass
d: Slow to 10 mph or less until you pass
exp: On a divided highway with a safety island or barrier, opposite traffic need not stop but must slow to no more than 10 mph.

q: How close may you follow a New Jersey emergency vehicle that is answering a call?
exp: No driver may follow a responding emergency vehicle closer than 300 feet.

q: How many points does passing a stopped school bus add to a New Jersey driving record?
exp: Improper passing of a school bus carries 5 points.

q: What is the minimum fine for a first offense of passing a stopped school bus in New Jersey?
exp: A first offense brings a fine of at least $100 and up to 15 days in jail or 15 days of community service.

q: Under New Jersey's Move Over law, what should you do when approaching a stopped tow truck with amber lights flashing?
a: Keep your lane and speed; tow trucks are not covered
b: Move over a lane, or slow down and be ready to stop
c: Stop behind the tow truck until it pulls away
d: Change lanes if a police car is also there
exp: The Move Over law covers emergency vehicles, tow trucks, highway maintenance and sanitation vehicles with flashing lights.

q: What is the fine range for violating New Jersey's Move Over law?
exp: A Move Over violation carries a fine of $100 to $500.

q: Does New Jersey's Move Over law protect a disabled car with its hazard lights flashing?
d: Yes, as well as one using flares or reflective triangles
exp: The law also covers disabled vehicles flashing hazard lights or using flares or reflective triangles.

q: Where must you pull over in New Jersey when an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren on?
a: To the right-hand edge or curb, clear of any intersection
b: To the nearest edge, left or right
c: Into the middle of the intersection
exp: State law directs drivers to the right-hand edge or curb, clear of intersections, stopping until it passes.

q: How close may you drive or park to New Jersey fire apparatus stopped in answer to a fire alarm?
exp: Drivers may not drive into or park within 200 feet of fire apparatus stopped for an alarm.

q: In New Jersey, you may not make a U-turn where your car cannot be seen from how far away in both directions?
exp: A U-turn is banned where the view of your car is blocked within 500 feet in either direction, and on curves and near hilltops.

q: For how far before a turn must you signal continuously in New Jersey?
exp: The turn signal must be given continuously for at least the last 100 feet before turning.

q: Where does New Jersey law ban U-turns?
b: On a curve or near the top of a hill
c: On any two-lane road at night
exp: U-turns are banned on curves, on the approach to or near the crest of a grade, where view is blocked within 500 feet, and where a NO U TURN sign is posted.

q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a New Jersey suburban business or residential district?
exp: New Jersey sets 35 mph in suburban business or residential districts.

q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit on New Jersey roads outside business, residential and school zones?
exp: The default limit in all other locations is 50 mph, except where higher limits are posted.

q: How many points does tailgating add to a New Jersey driving record?
exp: Following too closely carries 5 points.

q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a New Jersey business or residential district?
exp: New Jersey sets 25 mph in business and residential districts.

q: How many points does speeding 1 to 14 mph over the limit add in New Jersey?
exp: Speeding 1 to 14 mph over carries 2 points; 15 to 29 over carries 4; 30 or more carries 5.

q: How many points does speeding 15 to 29 mph over the limit add in New Jersey?
exp: Speeding 15 to 29 mph over carries 4 points.

q: How many points does speeding 30 mph or more over the limit add in New Jersey?
exp: Speeding 30 or more over the limit carries 5 points.

q: What is the highest speed limit posted on New Jersey highways?
exp: Under the 65 MPH Speed Limit Implementation Act, posted highway limits go up to 65 mph.

q: What minimum following distance does New Jersey's Division of Highway Traffic Safety teach in good weather?
exp: The state's tailgating campaign teaches at least 2 seconds in good weather, and 4 or 5 seconds when the road or weather is poor.

q: On a wet road or in poor weather, how much following distance does New Jersey's highway safety office advise?
exp: In poor road or weather conditions, increase the gap to 4 or 5 seconds.

q: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in New Jersey?
exp: New Jersey bans parking within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.

q: How close to a crosswalk at an intersection may you park in New Jersey, where there is no curb extension?
exp: Parking is banned within 25 feet of the nearest crosswalk or side line of an intersecting street.

q: How close to a stop sign may you park in New Jersey?
exp: New Jersey bans parking within 50 feet of a stop sign.

q: How close to the nearest rail of a railroad crossing may you park in New Jersey?
exp: Parking is banned within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

q: When parallel parking in New Jersey, how close to the curb must your wheels be?
exp: Park parallel to the edge of the road, headed with traffic, within 6 inches of it.

q: How close to a fire station driveway may you park on the same side of the street in New Jersey?
exp: Parking is banned within 20 feet of a fire station driveway, and within 75 feet on the opposite side where signs are posted.

q: When you pass a bicyclist in New Jersey and cannot change lanes, how much space must you leave?
exp: If a lane change is not possible, leave at least 4 feet while passing.

q: You approach a person walking on the road in New Jersey and can neither change lanes nor leave 4 feet. What must you do?
a: Slow to 25 mph or less and be ready to stop
b: Slow to 35 mph or less and pass with care
c: Pass at the posted limit with 3 feet
d: Stop and wait until the walker leaves the road
exp: When neither a lane change nor 4 feet of space is possible, slow to 25 mph or the lower posted limit and be prepared to stop.

q: What is New Jersey's first choice when passing a bicyclist on a road with two lanes in your direction?
d: Change into a lane not next to the bicyclist
exp: The law first asks drivers to change into a lane not adjacent to the person, when safe.

q: What is the penalty in New Jersey for an unsafe pass of a bicyclist that injures them?
d: A license suspension of one year
exp: Without injury the fine is $100 and no points; with bodily injury it is $500 and 2 points.

q: In New Jersey, a crash must be reported to police when property damage is more than what amount?
exp: Report any crash with injury, death or property damage over $500 to the police by the quickest means.

q: Within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle must you switch to low beams in New Jersey?
exp: Dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle comes within 500 feet.

q: When does New Jersey law require your headlights to be on during daytime rain?
a: When other drivers turn their lights on
b: Whenever the weather makes you use your wipers
c: When rain is heavy enough to flood the road
d: When driving on a highway in rain
exp: Lights are required whenever rain, mist, snow or other precipitation requires the use of wipers.

q: If no police officer files a report on a New Jersey crash that must be reported, how soon must you send a written report to the MVC?
exp: A written report goes to the MVC within 10 days unless an officer has filed one.

q: From when to when must headlights be on in New Jersey?
b: From one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
d: From a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise
exp: State law requires lights from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise.

q: In fog or smoke, New Jersey requires headlights when you cannot see people and vehicles how far ahead?
exp: Lights are required when there is not enough light to see persons and vehicles 500 feet ahead.

q: During a New Jersey traffic stop, which documents must you be able to show the officer?
c: Your license, registration and insurance card
exp: The driver must carry and show a license, registration certificate and insurance card on request.

q: What is the fine for failing to show your license, registration or insurance card to a New Jersey police officer?
exp: Failing to exhibit the required documents carries a $150 fine.

q: New Jersey's Attorney General advises what for a traffic stop at night?
c: Step out and walk to the police car
exp: The state's Safe Stop tips say to turn on the dome or interior light at night, roll down the window and keep your hands visible.

q: During a New Jersey traffic stop, what does the state say about questions after you hand over your documents?
b: You do not have to answer other questions
c: You must explain where you are going
exp: After providing your license, registration and insurance card, you have the right to remain silent on other questions.

q: At what BAC is a New Jersey driver under 21 in violation of the law?
exp: An under-21 driver with a BAC of 0.01 percent or more violates New Jersey's underage drinking and driving law.

q: Which phone use is allowed for a New Jersey driver with a basic license?
exp: Drivers may use a phone only hands-free, except to report an emergency such as a fire, crash or road hazard.

q: What is the fine range for a first hand-held phone offense in New Jersey?
exp: A first offense costs $200 to $400; a second $400 to $600; a third or later $600 to $800.

q: At what BAC is a New Jersey driver 21 or older considered drunk driving?
exp: A BAC of 0.08 percent or more is drunk driving for adult drivers.

q: What is the BAC limit for driving a commercial vehicle in New Jersey?
exp: Operating a commercial motor vehicle at 0.04 percent or more is illegal.

q: A New Jersey driver under 21 is convicted of driving with a BAC of 0.03. How long is the license suspension?
exp: Under-21 drivers at 0.01 to under 0.08 lose their license for 30 to 90 days and do 15 to 30 days of community service.

q: How many days of community service does an under-21 New Jersey driver with a BAC of 0.01 or more perform?
exp: The law requires 15 to 30 days of community service, plus the suspension and an alcohol education program.

q: A 16-year-old with no license is convicted of drinking and driving in New Jersey. When does the suspension begin?
a: When they become eligible for a license, or the conviction date if later
b: Immediately, and it ends before age 17
d: Never; there is no license to suspend
exp: The suspension starts on the date the person becomes eligible to get a license or the conviction date, whichever is later.

q: What is the minimum fine for a person under 21 who buys alcohol or lies about their age to buy it in New Jersey?
exp: Underage purchase or misrepresenting age to buy alcohol is a disorderly persons offense with a fine of at least $500.

q: What does New Jersey law give an underage person for a first offense of drinking or holding alcohol, with no car involved?
exp: A first violation brings a written warning from a law enforcement officer.

q: What is the fine for a first-time New Jersey driver who refuses a breath test after a drunk driving arrest?
exp: A first refusal costs $300 to $500, an Intoxicated Driver Resource Center class and the license until an ignition interlock is installed.

q: After a first refusal of a breath test in New Jersey, how long does the ignition interlock stay after the license is restored?
exp: For a refusal, the interlock remains 9 to 15 months after the license is returned.

q: What does a first-time New Jersey drunk driving offender with a BAC of 0.08 to under 0.10 have to install?
a: Nothing, if they pay the fine
exp: The license is lost until an interlock is installed, and the device stays for 3 months.

q: What is the fine range for a first New Jersey drunk driving offense with a BAC of 0.08 to under 0.10?
exp: The lowest BAC tier carries a fine of $250 to $400; higher tiers carry $300 to $500.

q: What yearly surcharge does the New Jersey MVC add after a first drunk driving conviction?
exp: The MVC surcharge for a first or second DWI is $1,000 a year for three years.

q: Who in a New Jersey car is banned from having an open container of alcohol?
d: No one, if the car is parked on the shoulder
exp: The open container law covers all occupants of a vehicle on a public highway, with exceptions such as charter bus and limousine passengers.

q: What is the fine for a first open container offense in New Jersey?
exp: A first offense costs $200; a later one $250 or 10 days of community service.

q: How many points does a third hand-held phone conviction add in New Jersey?
exp: A third or later offense adds 3 points and may bring a 90-day suspension.

q: May a New Jersey driver hold a phone to report a crash or a fire?
b: Yes, to report an emergency to the proper authorities
c: Only while stopped at a red light
exp: The law allows hand-held use to report a fire, traffic crash, serious road hazard or medical or hazardous materials emergency.

q: At how many points is a New Jersey driver's license suspended?
exp: A driver with 12 or more points on the current record faces suspension.

q: How must a New Jersey child under 2 who weighs less than 30 pounds ride?
b: In a rear-facing seat with a five-point harness
c: In a seat belt in the back seat
d: On an adult's lap in the back seat
exp: Children under 2 and under 30 pounds ride in a rear-facing seat with a five-point harness.

q: How often must a passenger car be inspected in New Jersey?
exp: Basic non-commercial vehicles are inspected every two years; new vehicles get a five-year first inspection.

q: Until when must a New Jersey child ride in a booster seat or harness seat?
exp: A child under 8 and under 57 inches rides in a harness seat until outgrown, then a booster seat.

q: Where must a child in a car seat ride in New Jersey, if the car has a back seat?
exp: Child restraints go in a rear seat; a front seat is allowed only without rear seats, and never rear-facing in front of an active airbag.

q: Which New Jersey passengers must wear seat belts?
a: The driver and front seat riders
b: Front seat riders and riders under 18
exp: Belts are required for the driver and front passengers, rear passengers 18 or older, and passengers 8 to 17; younger children use car seats.

q: What is the fine for a New Jersey seat belt violation?
exp: The seat belt fine is $20, and no points are assessed.

q: Who is responsible in New Jersey for making sure a 15-year-old passenger wears a seat belt?
b: The passenger's parent, wherever they are
d: The car's owner, even if not present
exp: The driver must secure passengers aged 8 to under 18 in a seat belt.

q: How many points come off a New Jersey driving record for each year with no violations or suspensions?
exp: One year without violations or suspensions removes 3 points.

q: How many points can a New Jersey state approved defensive driving course remove?
exp: A defensive driving course removes 2 points, once every five years.

q: How many points within three years trigger a New Jersey MVC surcharge?
exp: Six or more points within three years brings a $150 yearly surcharge, plus $25 for each point over six, for three years.

q: What is the minimum bodily injury liability for one person on a New Jersey standard auto policy?
exp: Standard policies issued or renewed now must carry at least $35,000 per person and $70,000 per crash for injuries, and $25,000 for property damage.

q: How much personal injury protection (PIP) does a New Jersey standard auto policy include at minimum?
exp: The lowest PIP option on a standard policy is $15,000 per person per accident.

q: Within how long must a New Jersey driver tell the MVC about a change of address?
exp: A licensed driver must notify the MVC within one week of moving.

q: What is the minimum property damage liability on a New Jersey standard auto policy?
exp: Standard policies must carry at least $25,000 in property damage liability.

q: A New Jersey driver under 21 arrives for the road test in a car without GDL decals. What happens?
a: The road test is not given
b: The examiner gives a warning and tests anyway
c: The driver pays a $4 fee at the car
d: The test is given on the off-road course only
exp: Missing decals are a reason the MVC denies a road test for drivers under 21.

q: Which of these is scored on the New Jersey road test?
exp: The skills tested include reverse driving, stops, corners, posture, steering, turning around, parallel parking and yielding.

q: Who must ride to the New Jersey road test with a permit holder?
a: Any licensed driver at least 18 with one year of experience
b: A New Jersey driver at least 21, licensed for three years
c: A certified driving instructor with a dual-brake car
d: No one; the permit holder may drive alone
exp: You must bring an accompanying New Jersey licensed driver at least 21 who has held a license for at least three years.

q: May a New Jersey road test applicant use a car's backup camera during the test?
c: Only with the examiner's written approval
d: Yes, backup cameras and parking sensors may be used
exp: The MVC allows backup cameras and parking sensors on the road test.

q: Which car will the New Jersey MVC refuse for a road test?
a: A car with an automatic transmission
b: A car with a backup camera
d: A car owned by a parent
exp: Self-parking vehicles, tinted windows, missing or expired inspection stickers and unsafe defects lead to denial.

q: Who may ride in the car during a New Jersey road test?
exp: For road tests, only the MVC examiner may ride in the car.

q: What does the examiner do when you pass the New Jersey road test?
a: Mails your probationary license within 10 days
b: Hands you a basic license before you leave
c: Schedules a second road test on a highway
d: Endorses your permit so you can get your license
exp: The examiner endorses the permit; you get the probationary license at the road test site, if it issues licenses, or any licensing center.

q: Where must the supervising driver sit while a New Jersey permit holder practices?
a: In the back seat behind the driver
d: In a separate car following behind
exp: The supervising driver sits in the front seat beside the permit holder.
